symptom: `ALTER ENTITY X ADD EVENT HANDLER …` errors when the handler exists and `DROP EVENT HANDLER …` errors when it does not, so a script containing either cannot be re-run — and a defensive drop-then-add fails on whichever half does not match. `ADD ATTRIBUTE` has `IF NOT EXISTS`; event handlers had no equivalent
cause: The idempotency guards added for attributes (findings #10) were never extended to the event-handler clauses, which are the one member with no other re-run route
insight: Reuse the existing `ifNotExists`/`ifExists` grammar rules rather than inventing a second spelling, so the guard reads the same everywhere. The error messages now name the flag, so the fix is discoverable from the failure. Verified by running the same script twice: first run drops (skipping, absent) then adds; second run skips both, exit 0, and the project still builds 0 errors. mxcli-todo #18
